settings.description: Memory the preloader may hold, in MB. auto: 70% of the memory free at the start, after keeping 4 GB for OMSI, at most 12 GB.
Shows the window that follows what is held in memory. It opens only when OmsiLaunch asks for it (this flag, /module-setting:omsi-prefetch.monitor=true, the settings file or a session profile).
Memory kept for OMSI when ram_budget_mb is auto, in MB.
Loading stops below this much free memory, in MB. auto: 2048, or 1024 with an explicit ram_budget_mb.
Cap, in MB, of what the map's AI vehicles and the user's vehicles may each hold. 0: only ram_budget_mb limits them.
Serves OMSI's byte-by-byte reads from 64 KiB blocks.
Collects OMSI's byte-by-byte writes of the terrain cache (.rdy) in 256 KiB blocks.
Opens assets below read_only_folders without write access.
Folders, relative to the OMSI folder and separated by ';', whose assets are opened read-only.
How far around the start and the player tiles are held, in tiles.
What of the map's AI vehicles is held.
Which of the user's vehicles are held.
Vehicle folders held with user_vehicles=list, separated by ';', in order.
What of each user vehicle is held.
What of each user vehicle carrying the map's timetable (.hof) is held.
Includes the sound files vehicles and objects cite.
Vehicle files opened ahead of the game without being held. list: the folders of pre_open_list.
What of each vehicle is opened ahead with pre_open all or list.
Vehicle folders opened ahead with pre_open list, separated by ';'.
Cold data, in MB, after which pre_open stops.
Threads of pre_open.
Cold data, in MB, after which the opening of a vehicle's folder on its first use stops.
Threads that open a vehicle's folder on its first use.
When a vehicle's preview starts, opens its folder ahead of the game.
Remembers what each session of a map used, to bring it in before the next one.
Reads the map's tiles to know what each one needs.
Shows a small window while a map is prepared for the first time, which explains the wait before OMSI opens.
Writes per-file and per-vehicle lines in the log. The normal log is a few dozen lines per session, at most 1 MiB per file, three files kept.
Limit of the module's data (what each map taught it): the maps used least recently are removed first.
